questions.subject: English
questions.stem:
It starts with a passion for a particular interest,
then comes the conviction that it is imperative to
realise it. Count the cost in years of effort, financial
investments and sacrifice. Then if it is still burning
in your blood and you are ready to commit yourself
to the task, plunge. It could be in any field—sports,
science, arts, business, or design. The road may be
uphill most of the way and often you are buoyed
up only by the knowledge that you are doing what
you love best and are doing the right thing. When
stamina is running out, the prospect of success will
keep you on track.

In the passage the road is called uphill and the writer says the one walking it is “buoyed up”; according to the passage, by what? (A) The prospect that the cost counted in years will one day be repaid (B) The support network that had earlier stood by the winner (C) The knowledge that you are doing what you love best and are doing the right thing (D) The certainty that the field is sports, science, arts, business or design

answerScheme.modelAnswer: The knowledge that you are doing what you love best and are doing the right thing

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: A mother is writing to her teenage daughter Ming, who has decided to give up a dream because the road looks uphill and the cost seems too high; write the letter in about 100 words, giving the date, a greeting, the message and a closing, and use it to persuade Ming to go on pursuing that dream.

markingPoints.description: Content: the letter persuades Ming to go on pursuing the dream instead of giving it up
Format: the letter shows the date, a greeting, the message and a closing
Organisation: the message moves in order from permission to follow, to the cost of the dream, to the encouragement to go on
Accuracy: the years of effort, financial investments and sacrifice, and the uphill road are described correctly
Expression: warm and clear language befitting a mother writing to her daughter, with no slang or abbreviations

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
19 June 1995

Dear Ming,

By all means follow that dream. I am glad you told me about it. The road may be uphill most of the way, but you are not alone on it. Count the cost in years of effort, financial investments and sacrifice, and then ask yourself whether you are ready to commit yourself to the task. If you are, plunge. When stamina runs out, the prospect of success will keep you on track, and doing what you love best and the right thing will buoy you up.

Love,
Mum

have a dream and they pursue it till it comes true.

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: Your school magazine wants a contribution of about 100 words for its column on students’ aims; write one paragraph on why it is important to follow a dream.

markingPoints.description: Content: at least two reasons for following a dream are given, such as the effort and sacrifice it demands and the strength it gives when the road is uphill
Format: the answer is a single paragraph of about 100 words, with no heading, letter layout or bullet points
Organisation: the reasons are arranged in a logical order, moving from what a dream demands to how it changes with life
Accuracy: the details are used correctly, such as at least ten years of singular and intensive pursuit and the prospect of success keeping a person on track
Expression: clear connected sentences using linkers such as because, since and also, with no repetition of the same idea

answerScheme.modelAnswer: Following a dream matters because the effort and the sacrifice behind it are what separate greatness from the ordinary. To reach world-class standard in any field, one has to pursue the subject singularly and intensively for at least ten years. A dream also gives a person a reason to carry on when the road is uphill, since the prospect of success will keep that person on track. Dreams are not fixed either, because life itself may change a person’s dreams, and these later hopes are no less than the original dream of younger days. Following a dream, then, is also how a person grows as life grows.

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: Your school is holding a week that encourages students to pursue their interests; write a speech of about 100 words for the school assembly, urging your schoolmates not to give up the dream they have chosen.

markingPoints.description: Content: the speech urges the assembly not to give up its dreams and gives the reason why great people succeed
Format: the speech opens with a greeting to the Principal, teachers and friends, and closes courteously with Thank you
Organisation: the points run in order from the cost of the dream, to the commitment it needs, to the support a dreamer never lacks
Accuracy: the details are used correctly, such as years of effort, financial investments and sacrifice, and the fields of sports, science, arts, business and design
Expression: clear spoken language addressed to the audience, with short sentences and no slang or abbreviations

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
Respected Principal, teachers and dear friends,

Good morning. Today I want to speak about why we must follow a dream. Great men and women become great because they have a dream and they pursue it till it comes true. The road will be uphill most of the way, so first count the cost in years of effort, financial investments and sacrifice. If the dream is still burning in your blood and you are ready to commit yourself to the task, plunge into it, whether it is sports, science, arts, business or design. Remember that no winner stands alone; there is always a group of people who stood by him or her. Follow your dream.

Thank you.

So, you see that for one winner, there is a
group of people who stood by him/her.

science, arts, business, or design.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: Step 1: She encourages by saying that great men and women become great because they have a dream and they pursue it till it comes true. Step 6: She also warns that life itself may change a person’s dreams, so the dream will take much longer to realise.

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: In her letter Ming’s mother says that the people who take part in a dream grow in number when the dream changes with life; explain in about 120 words, in steps, what she means by this.

markingPoints.description: Life itself may change a person’s dreams
The later hopes and aspirations are no less than the original dream of younger days
They must be realised by negotiating a path through a maze of hurdles
That makes the dream take a much longer time to realise
A longer, harder dream has many more participants, so the dreamscape grows larger
Her own example: publishing the book is a dream chased in the last ten years and is not the dream she had in her youth

answerScheme.modelAnswer: Step 1: A person’s original dream does not stay the same, because life itself may change a person’s dreams. Step 2: The hopes and aspirations that replace it are no less than the original dream of younger days, so they are still worth pursuing. Step 3: They are harder to realise, since you must negotiate a path through a maze of hurdles instead of a straight road. Step 4: For that reason the dream will take a much longer time to realise. Step 5: A longer and harder dream needs many more people, so the people who are participants in the dreamscape would be many more. Step 6: Her own case proves it: publishing the book is a dream she has chased in the last ten years, and it is not the dream she had in her youth.
